notes: Named Zosyn by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18: "I prefer generic names, but for combination products that can be a problem. Call it Zosyn." A brand name is a valid R name, as MEGX and MDMA are, so it needs no display name. "The PK should be labelled piperacillin": the drug is Zosyn, its curve is labelled piperacillin, and tazobactam is not plotted. Earlier decision of the same day: tazobactam is not a drug of its own, being given only in combination; the products are listed as "Piperacillin/tazobactam" and "Ceftolozane/tazobactam", each dosed in the units of its FDA label. This row and the next replace the planned stand-alone tazobactam. No new paper: stanpumpR's piperacillin (Kong 2025, R/drugs_piperacillin.R) already takes a dose of the product and plots piperacillin, tazobactam not plotted. The change: list it as Piperacillin/tazobactam and dose it in the Zosyn label's units, g of the combined product for adults (2.25, 3.375 and 4.5 g; 3.375 g q6h is 13.5 g a day, 12.0 g piperacillin + 1.5 g tazobactam, 8:1) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (90 mg/kg from 2 to 9 months, 80 piperacillin + 10 tazobactam; 112.5 mg/kg over 9 months), in place of today's mg pip-tazo. Renaming the drug piperacillin to Zosyn leaves links naming piperacillin to be mapped to it. Zhang 2021 and Chandorkar 2015, the largest tazobactam fits in nlmixr2lib, are ceftolozane-tazobactam fits and belong to the next row.

Ceftolozane/tazobactam. Named Zerbaxa by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18 ("Use Zerbaxa and Avycaz too", after naming Zosyn); its curve is labelled ceftolozane. The same decision of that day: dosed in the Zerbaxa label's units, g of the combined product for adults (1.5 g = 1 g ceftolozane + 0.5 g tazobactam, 2:1, q8h for cIAI and cUTI; 3 g for HABP/VABP) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (30 mg/kg = 20 ceftolozane + 10 tazobactam; 60 mg/kg; 75 mg/kg for HABP/VABP; each up to the adult dose). Plot ceftolozane, 2/3 of the dose, as piperacillin's product unit carries 4/4.5 (its doseProducts block); tazobactam not plotted. Source: Zhang 2021 (PMID 32949031, in the archive, read in full on the 2026-11-18 run for its tazobactam half), which fits both components; nlmixr2lib files its ceftolozane model as Zhang_2021_ceftolozane (968 participants). Label: DailyMed setid 70ac1d90-eff3-4f0b-9f46-5846c571b32f (May 2026). Still open: the infection state, a [decision] shared with imipenem: the model's volumes rise with the infection (pneumonia about doubles them) and stanpumpR has no infection field.

Imipenem-cilastatin (and imipenem-relebactam). Weekly run 2026-11-18: the pick Patel 2022 (PMID 34704389, in the archive, read in full) gives Table 3: CL 12.7 L/h x (CrCl/105.5)^0.48 x (WT/75)^0.29 x (1 - 0.38 pneumonia), V1 11.4 x (WT/75)^1.03 L x (1 - 0.39 pneumonia) x (1 + 0.23 ventilated), V2 7.79 L, Q 23.1 L/h; reference healthy/cIAI/cUTI; CrCl by Cockcroft-Gault. Blocked on papers, not a decision: (a) its Supplementary Methods (PMC8841461, CTS-15-396-s001.docx; PMC refused the scripted download) define the Cockcroft-Gault weight and any cap; save as PMID_34704389_sup1.docx; (b) the antibiotic band needs an imipenem MBC/MIC ratio and a plain-imipenem P. aeruginosa MIC50/90: Edwards 1989 (PMID 2655530, AAC 33:215, no text in PMC) for the ratio, and a surveillance paper reporting imipenem alone for P. aeruginosa (Shortridge 2022, PMID 35262394, reports only imipenem-relebactam). Enterobacterales imipenem MIC50/90 is in hand: <=0.12/1 mg/L, ESBL <=0.12/0.5 (Sader 2023, PMID 36861086, Table 2). Pneumonia (CL x 0.62, V1 x 0.61) is not applied: no infection field; a [decision] for Shafer if he wants one.
